assessment.nobel_worthiness: Direct observation of the Higgs boson closed the Standard Model's scalar sector and verified the mechanism whose theory was recognised in 2013. It is a clear, specific, lasting experimental milestone, and the later coupling measurements make the discovery's meaning stable.
assessment.attribution: Credit is inherently collective across two collaborations of thousands. Of the four credited names, the founding-era leaders of ATLAS and CMS (Jenni, Della Negra) and the spokesperson at the time of the announcement (Gianotti) are a defensible trio, but this omits Virdee and any CMS counterpart, so the allocation is contestable and any three-person choice is partly arbitrary.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed independently by two experiments and by years of Run 2 and Run 3 data; the 2013 prize already stressed the theory, so experimental recognition is overdue rather than premature.
uncertainties: Whether the statutes' three-person limit can fairly represent two collaborations is unresolved.
My choice among the four credited names rests on remembered roles, not verified detail.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The optical lattice clock, built on Katori's magic-wavelength proposal, reaches fractional uncertainties near 1e-18 and underpins redefinition of the second, tests of fundamental constants and relativistic geodesy. This is a concrete invention with demonstrated, growing impact.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed the magic-wavelength lattice concept and realised early clocks; Ye's group drove the performance records and many-body-clock work. Two laureates is a coherent configuration; others (for example Hall and Hansch combs) were already honoured in 2005.
assessment.maturity: Many independent laboratories confirm the performance; the timing is good, though the formal redefinition of the second is still pending.
uncertainties: Relative weighting of Katori's conceptual proposal and Ye's later performance advances may be disputed.
Other contributors such as Takamoto or Lemonde are outside the supplied credit.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Circuit QED created the architecture for strong coupling of single microwave photons to superconducting qubits and now underlies most superconducting quantum processors. It is original, clear and demonstrably transformative for quantum technology and for quantum optics on a chip.
assessment.attribution: Blais, Wallraff and Schoelkopf form the theory proposal plus first experiments and the later circuit-QED development. The credited trio is natural, though the 2025 prize for macroscopic quantum tunnelling in circuits shows overlapping recognition in the broader field and the allocation vs the transmon inventors is a question.
assessment.maturity: Highly mature and independently reproduced across many groups, with a steady growth of quantum-processor milestones.
uncertainties: Overlap with earlier superconducting-circuit recognition may limit appetite for another prize in this area.
Whether transmon or other device inventors belong beside the credited names is unclear from the supplied data.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The KPZ class is a cornerstone of non-equilibrium statistical physics, linking growth, directed polymers and interface roughening to exact results in random-matrix theory (Tracy-Widom statistics). Its exact solutions and the careful experimental confirmation in liquid-crystal turbulence give an unusual blend of deep theory and measurement. From my own field, the conceptual impact on understanding universality far from equilibrium is large.
assessment.attribution: Kardar, Parisi and Zhang wrote the 1986 equation; Parisi is not in the supplied credit and already holds the 2021 prize, which complicates a fair configuration. Takeuchi's experiments are decisive for the experimental confirmation, while the mathematical exact solutions (Johansson, Prahofer-Spohn, Sasamoto-Spohn, Amir-Corwin-Quastel) are not credited here.
assessment.maturity: Theory dates to 1986 and precise experiments to 2010-2011, with ongoing 1D and higher-dimensional confirmation; recognition is timely but partial.
uncertainties: The missing exact-solution contributors make the supplied credit incomplete.
Whether a prize for statistical-physics universality sits comfortably within the Nobel physics tradition is a judgement call.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Wavefront shaping and time reversal show that multiple scattering is deterministic, invertible information rather than irreversible loss, enabling focusing and imaging through disorder. This connects deeply with random-matrix transmission eigenchannels and has applications in imaging and acoustic therapy.
assessment.attribution: Vellekoop and Mosk made the 2007 optical wavefront-shaping demonstration, and Fink pioneered time-reversal acoustics. The credited trio is coherent but joins two partly separate lineages, and Dorokhov-style transmission-eigenchannel theory is not credited.
assessment.maturity: Good independent confirmation in optics, acoustics and microwaves; practical impact in biomedical imaging is still developing.
uncertainties: Compound discovery spanning acoustics and optics may need distinct recognition.
Magnitude of the field's fundamental, rather than applied, impact is somewhat uncertain.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The jamming picture gives a unifying, critical-like description of the onset of rigidity in grains, foams and glasses, with scaling exponents and isostaticity that organise disordered matter. It is original and conceptually influential in soft matter and in glassy physics.
assessment.attribution: Liu and Nagel proposed the jamming phase diagram, and O'Hern with Silbert, Liu and Nagel gave the numerical point-J analysis; Silbert is not credited, and the theoretical mean-field solution (Parisi, Zamponi and colleagues) is outside the list. The proposed trio is plausible but leaves clear gaps.
assessment.maturity: Several experiments and simulations support the picture, but its exact universality class and relation to the glass transition remain debated.
uncertainties: Debate about whether jamming is a true critical point limits maturity.
Credit overlap with mean-field glass theory is unresolved.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Ultracold atoms in optical lattices realised Hubbard models cleanly and allow quantum simulation of many-body physics, starting from the superfluid-Mott transition and now reaching quantum-gas microscopy. The work links condensed-matter theory and controlled experiments in an important way.
assessment.attribution: Zoller and Jaksch proposed the Hubbard realisation; Greiner and Bloch observed the Mott transition; Esslinger realised fermionic Mott states. Choosing three of the four credited names is hard, and omitting Greiner is a notable judgement call, while Jaksch is outside the supplied credit.
assessment.maturity: Strongly confirmed by many labs, though the central question, whether quantum simulation resolves open questions such as d-wave superconductivity, is not yet answered.
uncertainties: Maturity of scientific payoff in answering open Hubbard-model questions is uncertain.
Choice among four credited names is difficult and partly arbitrary.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The prediction and observation of the quantum spin Hall state introduced a time-reversal-invariant topological phase and helped launch topological insulators and a broad range of topological materials research. The impact on condensed-matter physics is large and enduring.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele made the original proposal and Molenkamp's group observed the effect in HgTe wells after the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang prediction. The supplied credit leaves out Zhang and the 3D topological insulator discoverers (Hasan, Moore, Fu), so a fair configuration is uncertain.
assessment.maturity: Well confirmed, with years of independent work, but the 2016 prize on topological phases partly overlaps the field, which may reduce the appetite for another award.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2016 prize and with candidate B014 may complicate separate recognition.
Omitted contributors weaken the supplied credit.
